lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: # Comprehende

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: This is a tool that helps us, humans understand (comprehend) AI code changes, such as PR diffs, or per-turn changes, or any diff that we define. Reading PR diffs line by line, in alphabetical order never made sense, and it's time we do something about it, provide us with a way of reviewing code changes in a scalable, easy to digest form, without losing on fidelity.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ## Background

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: AI agents write more code than humans can review line by line. This tool moves review from cognitive surrender to cognitive offloading. The glossary below defines both. The full argument is in the README.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ## What the tool is

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: It's a review assistant tool, which users can run as a skill (invoked using slash command). This will take a diff (PR, turn diff, or anything needing a review), analyze it, find review groups and visualize them on a web UI.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ### Goals

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - 100% accuracy: live git wins. The review document is interpretation only.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - Easy on the eyes, easy to read

lines.author: Cursor Agent
lines.text: - Allow drilling down to full files instead of the diff, git blames, commit messages, branches, and the sources the skill read

lines.author: Cursor Agent
lines.text: - Useful summaries of the issues and other sources.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - UI is always the same, not generated on the fly. Only the data changes.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - Works locally, no need for hosted services, deployed packages

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - Simple easy-to-understand wording throughout the UI and in the generated answers, using ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ## Glossary

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ### Concepts

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: **Cognitive offloading.** Hand off the _how_. Keep the _why_ and the _what_. The human still has a view of the change to compare against.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: **Cognitive surrender.** Stop constructing an answer and adopt the tool's answer, with no _why_ or _what_ of your own. That is how comprehension debt grows.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: **Comprehension debt.** The gap between the code in the system and the understanding the humans who develop, maintain, or operate it have. Unlike technical debt, nobody chooses it. It stays invisible until something breaks.

lines.author: Cursor Agent
lines.text: **The title.** Short name for the whole change. Always written. Prefer a user-created title (pull request, ticket, transcript) when it names this change. Invent one when that title is missing, vague, or names something else.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: **The why.** Why this work exists. The skill writes it from tickets, issues, PR comments, coding-agent transcripts and any existing human or agent generated that's related to the change. One for the whole change when those sources name one story. Omit it when they are silent or mixed. One on every group. A group with no source of its own may exist to enable later groups. Do not invent a motive from the patch.

lines.author: Cursor Agent
lines.text: **The what.** What this change is. Always written. Document `summary` is the whole change. Group `summary` is that group. Named so a human has a view before they read the diff.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: **The how.** How the change is implemented. The live git diff is the how. The agent may group and summarize it. The agent must not replace it.

lines.author: Cursor Agent
lines.text: **Look for.** Claims the live diff does not make obvious. Group `lookFor` holds claims that live in those hunks. Document `lookFor` holds whole-change and missing-work claims. Cite the source. Do not store a pass/fail. The skill writes the comparison; the field is only the place for it.

lines.author: Cursor Agent
lines.text: **Source.** A ticket, pull request, PR comment, commit, or transcript the skill read to write its prose. Locators plus a gist. PR comments also copy author, body, and an optional line pin. Transcripts have no URL.

lines.author: Cursor Agent
lines.text: **Citation.** A markdown link `[text](source:id)` in the why, the what, or lookFor. The UI turns it into a mark. `validate` fails on an unknown id.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ### Code

lines.author: Cursor Agent
lines.text: **Review document.** Interpretation only. Title, groups, summaries, optional generated why, optional lookFor, sources, hunk pointers. Never patch text. Source refs must resolve in cwd.

lines.author: Cursor Agent
lines.text: **Group.** Schema `groups` item. The UI uses the same word.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: **Review concern.** Why these hunks are read together. Not a directory, unless that directory is the concern.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: **Part / story.** Independent work. Could have been its own PR. `dependsOn` only inside a story.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: **Size.** Review burden. Not file or hunk count.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: **Hunk ref.** Pointer into live git. Copy from `index`. Never invent.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: **Index.** Hunk list for the agent. No line content. Not stored in the UI.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: **Live git.** `git` in cwd at serve time. Git wins.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: **Coverage.** Every live hunk in at least one group. Duplicates allowed.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: **Unassigned.** Live hunks with no group. Still shown.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: **Stale ref.** Pointer that does not match live git. Serve still starts. Do not invent a replacement.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: **Skill.** Grouping instructions. Does not talk to git.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: **CLI.** Git, validate, serve. Cwd is the repo.

lines.author: Cursor Agent
lines.text: ## Project rules

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: Skill edits go in `skills-next/comprehende/`. `pnpm release:skill` writes `skills/comprehende/` and `pnpm sync:skill` writes `.agents/skills/comprehende/`. Leave both alone. Edit source under `src/` normally.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: Component look lives on the component. Tailwind first. If a bit of CSS is required, colocate it with that component using a CSS module. A component must not import a global stylesheet. Do not add descendant selectors in `styles.css` to style markup a component already owns. `styles.css` holds globals such as variables and themes. Exception: `src/ui/lib/gap-style.ts` may use descendant selectors to style Pierre markup.

lines.author: Cursor Agent
lines.text: If the UI already shows the state, do not add a sentence that narrates it.

lines.author: Cursor Agent
lines.text: README is for people using the tool. Change it when a command, install step, or other user-visible behavior changes. Leave it alone for internal implementation.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: Type safety helps humans and agents alike. Parse at the boundary, where the schema is the source of truth, and infer everywhere inside. If a bug could have been a type error, make it one before fixing it.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: Releases happen manually. Do not change `package.json` version unless the user asks for a release. When they do, follow the Release section in [README.md](./README.md).

lines.author: Cursor Agent
lines.text: ## Pull requests

lines.author: Cursor Agent
lines.text: When opening a pull request, run the comprehende skill from skills-next on that PR using the local built CLI, export the review, then publish it with `pnpm exec tsx scripts/pages-review.ts publish --dir "$EXPORT_DIR" --pr <number>`. Put the printed URL in the PR body.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ## Notes from Máté, the repo owner

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: I love to see simple code solving real, complex problems. Make every change, design, and text in that spirit. The skill is reviewed and adjusted by me manually, but write it with these principles in mind too.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: I don't want this project to get overly complicated. In practice this means I want to keep the code focusing on the universal Git part, not specifics of any Git forge or issue tracker - those must be handled at the skill level.

lines.author: Cursor Agent
lines.text: Watch out for small, quick neat wins and the attention to detail that makes people say wow, that's cool.
